text:
alex: heads-up — customer reported intermittent p95 spikes on /embeddings when they send a mix of tiny realtime calls and a few large batched uploads. looks like routing is oversubscribing the same GPU pool and small requests wait for batch windows. :eyes:
maria: ugh. can you paste an example payload + headers? curious about dims and any custom headers.
alex: sure — simplified example:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -H 'X-Embed-Dims: 1536' \\n  -d '{"inputs": ["tiny text"], "client_request_id": "r123"}'
```
We also saw them send large arrays (~12k entries) in parallel from a batch worker. small calls get queued behind the batch.
jamal: this is the contracts vs realtime problem we've talked about — our preflight/route decision currently treats mixed-dim or large payloads as "batch" and funnels to batch pool. That preserves throughput but kills tail latency for tiny calls.
sophie: adding a realtime fastpath is fine but we need to think quota + Dedicated capacity implications. fastpath shouldn't let a tenant blow past reserved capacity. otherwise we get noisy neighbors.
jamal: agree. proposal: add an explicit header to opt into realtime fastpath (X-Embed-Mode: realtime|batch|auto). default remains auto (current behavior). Console exposes a per-route toggle prefer_realtime that maps to a tenant-level policy. Also add a server-side soft quota check that rejects >N tokens on the realtime pool.
maria: telemetry needed: a tag on requests indicating chosen route, queue_time_ms, and whether preflight coerced dims. dashboard: per-tenant p50/p95 for both pools + a counter for "route_override". we should surface in the console so SRE and customers can see.
jamal: simple rollout plan: feature-flag the header handling -> internal canary -> enable for a small % of tenants (console toggle) -> monitor travel time metrics. add an alarm if p95 realpath > baseline * 1.5.
sophie: also add a preflight that fast-fails too-large realtime requests with 413 + hint to use batch (and response body with suggested chunk-size). don't forget quota enforcement: realtime route should still decrement tokens against tenant quota atomically.
alex: can we also add a short-circuit to prefer local KV prefix cache for realtime path (avoid disk fetches)? that might keep p95 stable.
jamal: yep, runtime already exposes a cache hint. we need a knob to prefer cache-on-hit for X-Embed-Mode=realtime.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: embed-routing-canary v2 -> prod at 2024-10-19T18:30Z (canary on 5% tenant slice).
deploy-bot: canary created, dashboard links: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/embeds/route-canary-172945 (auto-generated).
maria: owners? who picks up console toggle + dashboard panels?
sophie: i'll own the console pieces + quota enforcement. tagging @jamal for runtime route changes and @alex for SDK header docs. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks — i'll draft SDK patch to add X-Embed-Mode and a short migration note for customers that rely on low tail latency.
jamal: i'll add telemetry keys: route_choice, queue_time_ms, dimension_hint, preflight_reason. we'll also emit a metric embed_route_switches{from="auto",to="realtime"}. :thinking_face:
sophie: quick checklist before canary: unit tests for header parsing, preflight 413 behavior, quota decrement verification, console toggle UI + permissions, dashboard panels + alerts.
alex: sounds good. i'll open PRs for SDK and a short playbook for oncall.
maria: perfect — meet in the morning standup to walk through the rollout steps.
